item.text: The recovery pass found several materially useful exact-locator sources. In particular, the 2000 U.S. State Department report supplies direct attribution boundaries (Federal Police report to the Interior Minister; provincial police to governors), names de la Rúa’s two judicial nominations and Senate non-confirmation, documents the April labor-reform protest, press harassment, women’s representation, NGO cooperation, and unresolved wiretap legislation. CRS and Freedom House independently corroborate the coalition/bribery response; ICJ and IPI add judicial and media detail; CELS adds a civil-society account of protest and institutional violence. I’m now checking whether the manifest can be patched despite the shell failure.

Research continuation completed without scoring.

I recovered and split the following defensible units:

- `R3E001` — State Department 2000 report: 1999 elections were considered free and fair; exact report overview. Supports 4B.1, 4B.8, 4B.10.
- `R3E002` — Federal Police reported to the Interior Minister; provincial police to governors. Establishes attribution boundaries for police abuses. Supports 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.10. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E003` — De la Rúa nominated two federal judges from Magistrates Council lists; neither was confirmed by the Senate. Supports 4B.4 and 4B.10. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E004` — April labor-reform protest: federal police clashes injured more than 30 demonstrators, including rubber-bullet injuries. Supports 4B.3 and 4B.10; does not establish presidential ordering. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E005` — Government generally respected speech and press rights, but public officials harassed, threatened, and criticized journalists. Supports 4B.6. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E006` — Wiretap-control proposals remained unenacted in 2000; authorized wiretaps continued under a Menem-era decree. Supports 4B.9 and 4B.10. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E007` — Gender quotas increased women’s congressional representation; only two of 72 senators were women and no Supreme Court justice was a woman. Supports 4B.7. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E008` — Human-rights groups operated without government restriction; government cooperation was general but not always responsive. Supports 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.10. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/25982)
- `R3E009` — De la Rúa created an Anti-Corruption Bureau, investigated former-official wrongdoing, and tightened disclosure rules. Supports 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.10. [Source](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/RS20781.html)
- `R3E010` — He retained two officials associated with the Senate scandal; Vice President Álvarez resigned in protest. Supports 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.8, 4B.10. This is direct response evidence, not proof of bribery. [Source](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/RS20781.html)
- `R3E011` — ICJ reported continuing political influence over provincial courts while describing the new Magistrates Council as a partial institutional improvement. Supports 4B.4 and 4B.10. [Source](https://www.icj.org/wp-content/uploads/2001/08/argentina_attacks_justice_2000.pdf)
- `R3E012` — CELS characterized 2000 national-government responses to organized roadblocks as repression and criminalization of union delegates and unemployed workers. Supports 4B.3 and 4B.10; attribution is to government policy, not necessarily the president personally. [Source](https://www.cels.org.ar/web/capitulos/criminalizacion-y-represion-de-las-protestas-sociales/)
- `R3E013` — IPI reported subtle improvement in the national government’s press-freedom approach while documenting continuing intimidation by locally connected actors. Supports 4B.6 and 4B.10. [Source](https://www.infoamerica.org/documentos_pdf/ipi_ar_00.pdf)

The Senate material remains carefully separated:

- allegation and legislative context;
- coalition and executive-response consequences;
- retention of implicated officials;
- later acquittal because evidence did not exceed reasonable doubt.

No claim of proven presidential bribery is retained.

I also verified the previously supplied HRW units, including the April 19 Federal Police suppression, European prosecutions not obstructed by the administration, provincial abuses, and journalist threats. [HRW source](https://www.hrw.org/legacy/wr2k1/americas/argentina.html)

The manifest update could not be persisted: both shell access and `apply_patch` failed with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`. The required additions are `R3E001`–`R3E013`; existing bundled `R2E005` should be split and retained only as contextual evidence. No score or ranking conclusion was produced.
